title: 5-repo-diverse-corpus

dependencyPrep.notes: Pre-built binary used as instructed; build: false passed to run_corpus.

findings: 89 parsing failures across corpus — consistent with binary/non-text config files (images, compiled artifacts) being discovered but unable to parse
55 validation issues from schema mismatches; no schema fetch errors (SchemaStore matched successfully)
0 crashes, 0 unexplained warnings — clean run with exit code 1 only due to real issues found
Skipped 771 of 2105 discovered files — skip rate of ~37%, suggesting a large number of non-config or unsupported file types in large polyglot repos like gitea and neovim
gitea (Go/TypeScript monorepo) likely contributes most parsing failures due to volume of diverse config files
pnpm monorepo (TypeScript/Node) likely yields rich package.json and tsconfig validation findings
fastapi (Python) likely minimal findings due to simpler pyproject.toml/setup.cfg schema coverage
neovim (C/Lua) likely has CMake and Lua config files that are parsed but may lack schema coverage

productRecommendations.recommendation: Improve parsing error messaging to distinguish binary/non-text files from genuinely malformed configs — 89 parsing failures in 5 repos suggests many false positives
productRecommendations.rationale: High parsing failure count (89) relative to validated (1245) indicates the parser is attempting to parse non-text or binary files that should be excluded before parsing, leading to noisy output

productRecommendations.recommendation: Audit skip logic — 771 skipped of 2105 discovered (37%) is high; confirm skip reasons are reported and the skip rate is expected for polyglot monorepos
productRecommendations.rationale: Large skip rate could indicate over-broad file discovery or under-coverage of config file types relevant to Go, Lua, and C ecosystems present in gitea and neovim

productRecommendations.recommendation: Add schema coverage for Lua-based config files (e.g., neovim plugin specs, stylua.toml) to improve C/Lua ecosystem support
productRecommendations.rationale: neovim uses Lua-based config heavily; without coverage, the tool provides limited value for C/Lua projects

followUp: Deep-dive the per-file artifact when accessible to classify which repos contribute most parsing failures vs. validation issues
Consider adding gitea as a regression target for Go+YAML config validation (large, diverse, active)
pnpm monorepo is a strong future candidate for package.json/tsconfig deep validation testing
